relations.subject: Hakuyū Taizan Maezumi
relations.evidence: in high school began studying koans under a lay Rinzai instructor, Koryū Osaka... receiving his inka in 1973.

relations.subject: Hakuyū Taizan Maezumi
relations.role: degrees in oriental literature and philosophy
relations.evidence: While studying under Koryu he attended Komazawa University—receiving degrees in oriental literature and philosophy.

relations.subject: Hakuyū Taizan Maezumi
relations.evidence: After college he trained at Sōji-ji

relations.subject: Hakuyū Taizan Maezumi
relations.evidence: received shihō from his father in 1955, a standard procedure in the Soto-sect

relations.subject: Hakuyū Taizan Maezumi
relations.evidence: In 1956 he was sent to the United States to serve as a priest at the Zenshuji Soto Mission in Little Tokyo, Los Angeles

relations.subject: Hakuyū Taizan Maezumi
relations.evidence: In 1959, he took classes in English at San Francisco State University

relations.subject: Hakuyū Taizan Maezumi
relations.evidence: Also in 1967, Maezumi began koan-study with Hakuun Yasutani, who had left the Soto-sect, completing kōan study under him and receiving his inka (dharma transmission) in 1970.

relations.subject: Hakuyū Taizan Maezumi
relations.object: Kuroda Institute for the Study of Buddhism and Human Values
relations.evidence: In 1976, Maezumi founded the non-profit Kuroda Institute for the Study of Buddhism and Human Values, promoting academic scholarship on Buddhist topics.
